# StatusPan

> StatusPan is an open-source local board for which AI agent is working on what. One Go binary listens on loopback. Agents push job updates and never get a callback. A self-hosted Cloudflare relay is optional for agents on another machine. Version 0.3.0.

Quick install, then serve. The board is at http://127.0.0.1:4477.

On macOS, [StatusPan.dmg](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg) is a WKWebView window on the local board. It starts the bundled `statuspan serve` if nothing answers on `STATUSPAN_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1:4477`), and it stops only a daemon it started.

The CLI works on macOS and Linux and installs to `~/.local/bin/statuspan`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://statuspan.com/install.sh | sh
statuspan serve
```

Post one update. The CLI posts to the relay when `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` are set, and to the local daemon otherwise.

```bash
statuspan post --agent "My Agent" --job build-1 --state running --progress 40
```

As a backup, you can always use the URL with plain curl, as long as the URL is the one where StatusPan is actually running.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "${STATUSPAN_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:4477/api/jobs}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"agent":"My Agent","job_id":"build-1","state":"running","progress":40}'
```

## Protocol

- States you can post: `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `done`, `failed`.
- `stalled` and `abandoned` are derived when the board is read. Bots cannot post them.
- A running job with no heartbeat for `ttl` seconds (default 600) is stalled. Queued, blocked, done, and failed do not stall.
- The latest `seq` for an `(agent, job_id)` wins. An equal or older seq stays in history and does not change the job. Omit `seq` and the post applies.
- Partial updates merge. Omitted fields stay as they are. A new job needs `state`. A later post may omit it.
- Fire and forget. If StatusPan is offline, keep working. Do not block the real job on the post.
- Healthy recurring jobs and scheduled routines stay off the board. Do not clutter it with daily or hourly runs that are going fine. If a recurring job becomes `blocked` (it needs human input or approval) or `failed`, push it so it surfaces in Needs attention. Once it is fixed or unblocked, push `done` so it clears out of Needs attention. Use `blocked` only when you actually asked a human.

## CLI

- `statuspan agent` prints the skill that ships in the binary. `statuspan agent prompt` prints a short snippet for AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. `statuspan agent json` prints a discovery document. `statuspan agent install` writes the skill into agent directories (`--target auto|agents|claude|cursor|codex|all`, `--dir`, `--home`, `--dry-run`).
- `statuspan run --agent NAME --job ID [--title T] [--recurring] -- COMMAND` posts `running`, heartbeats, then `done` or `failed`, and exits with the command's status. `--recurring` posts nothing on success and one `failed` on a non-zero exit. A command that cannot start is exit 127 and one `failed` post.
- `STATUSPAN_AGENT` is the default for `run --agent`. `STATUSPAN_URL` is the full local jobs endpoint for `post` and `run` (for example `http://127.0.0.1:14477/api/jobs`). `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` is a file containing the relay write token, used when `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` is unset.
- The same recurring rule applies to the CLI: healthy routines stay off the board. Push `blocked` or `failed` when a routine needs a person or has failed, then push `done` once it is resolved.

## Self-host the relay

Cloud and remote agents (Cursor cloud agents, CI, other servers) cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on your machine. They post to a relay with a write token stored as a secret. The local daemon pulls those jobs in. If you do not want to run Cloudflare yourself, use Hosted Relay: https://statuspan.com/cloud.

A free Cloudflare account and Node.js are enough. From `relay/`:

```bash
cd relay
npm install
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy
openssl rand -hex 32 > admin-token
npx wrangler secret put ADMIN_TOKEN < admin-token
chmod 600 admin-token
export RELAY_URL=https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(cat admin-token)
node scripts/admin.mjs create-workspace home
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind write --agent MyBot --label laptop --out write-token
node scripts/admin.mjs mint home --kind read --label board --out read-token
chmod 600 write-token read-token
```

`wrangler deploy` prints the `workers.dev` URL. Never commit `admin-token`. A write token posts for one agent and cannot read the board. A read token feeds the board and cannot post. The admin token creates workspaces and mints, lists, and revokes tokens. Never give it to bots.

Point the daemon at the relay with `relay.json` in the data directory (macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/statuspan/relay.json`):

```json
{"url":"https://statuspan-relay.<account>.workers.dev","workspace":"home","read_token":"<paste the read token>"}
```

`chmod 600` that file and restart the daemon. It polls about every 3 seconds. Alternative env: `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_RELAY_READ_TOKEN`.

Agents post with `STATUSPAN_RELAY_URL`, `STATUSPAN_RELAY_WORKSPACE`, and `STATUSPAN_TOKEN_FILE` (or `STATUSPAN_TOKEN` as a secret), then `statuspan post` or `statuspan run`, or curl with `Authorization: Bearer`.

Full steps: https://statuspan.com/relay and https://statuspan.com/llms-full.txt.

## Specs

- [Full reference](https://statuspan.com/llms-full.txt): CLI, HTTP API, relay, and copy-paste clients
- [Self-host the relay](https://statuspan.com/relay): Cloudflare Worker setup, tokens, and `relay.json`
- [Hosted Relay](https://statuspan.com/cloud): no-setup relay, waitlist
- [Agent skill](https://statuspan.com/skill.md): drop-in instructions for a coding agent
- [OpenAPI](https://statuspan.com/openapi.json): local daemon and self-hosted relay
- [Job update schema](https://statuspan.com/schema/job-update.schema.json): JSON Schema for one update or a batch
- [Mac app](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest/download/StatusPan.dmg): StatusPan.dmg, universal, macOS 12 or later
- [Installer](https://statuspan.com/install.sh): macOS and Linux, no sudo, installs to `~/.local/bin/statuspan`
- [Releases](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan/releases/latest): CLI binaries and StatusPan.dmg
- [Source](https://github.com/kirillzubovsky/statuspan): MIT
